sources.citation: OLAC aggregated catalogue, nightly dump 18 July 2021 (local copy): all records coded mze or mentioning Morawa/Mailuan.
sources.note: Only 5 mze records (Ethnologue, Rosetta Swadesh list, Capell vocabulary notes PARADISEC AC2-OLVOC606, Glottolog, transnewguinea.org). SIL Language & Culture Archives lists only 'Bauwaki Wordlist' 1973 (id 56500) for the sister language; no Morawa OPD, survey report or sketch.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. Morawa Swadesh List (archive.org item rosettaproject_mze_swadesh-1, uploaded 2010).
sources.note: Plain wordlist, no stress marks, no source named.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1975. South-Eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 613-664. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 2.9.5.5 p.638: 'None of the languages except Magi (or Mailu) has been studied or recorded in any detail.' Sec. 2.9.5.5.3 Morawa (p.639): territory and four villages only. Only a phylum-wide remark p.622 ('Some languages are tonal but stress is generally important and related to intonation'), nothing Morawa-specific.

sources.citation: Greenhill, S. J. TransNewGuinea.org, 'Morawa' language page (56 lexical items) sourced from 'Summer Institute of Linguistics Language Survey of Bauwake and Morawa, 1973'.
sources.note: Wordlist only, no stress marks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record mora1273 (Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less; refs: Anonymous 1913, 1914 Papua Annual Report vocabularies; Grist 1926; Bastard 1918; Dutton 1975, 1982, 1999; Ray 1938).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; zero grammar/phonology/sketch entries.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2017. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide (The World of Linguistics 4), 21-195. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton. Open access chapter, OAPEN handle 20.500.12657/23719.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing on Morawa phonology. The Mailuan subsection (extracted text) gives location, cognate percentages (c.50%, Dutton 1999), a documentation listing per language -- 'Morawa [mze] 1,100; wordlist: Anonymous 1913, 1914b, Ray 1938' versus 'Mailu (Magi) [mgu].. grammar sketches: Lanyon-Orgill 1944, Saville 1912, Thomson 1975' -- Ross's Proto-Mailuan pronouns and a few pTNG reflexes in Mailu/Bauwaki. It thus independently confirms that no phonological description of Morawa exists; the chapter's tone/stress remarks concern other TNG groups (e.g. Chimbu-Wahgi tone), not Mailuan.

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom. 1996. Lau'una: another Austronesian remnant on the south-east coast of Papua. Pacific Linguistics C-133:61-82. (ANU hdl 1885/253876)
sources.note: Concerns Ray's 'Lauuna' (earlier lumped with Morawa) which is Austronesian; Morawa appears only as neighbour/loan source. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom. 1982. Borrowing in Austronesian and non-Austronesian languages of coastal south-east mainland Papua New Guinea. In A. Halim, L. Carrington & S. A. Wurm (eds), Papers from the Third International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics, vol. 1: Currents in Oceanic, 109-177. Pacific Linguistics C-74. Canberra: ANU. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/253270)
sources.note: Appendix 2 (pp.162-163) gives tentative synchronic phoneme inventories for all Mailuan languages incl. Morawa (5 vowels; p/f, t/s, k, b, d, g, h, m, n, l/r, v/w, y; open syllables, no clusters, final-vowel loss after nasals; fn.42 n spreading to replace r in Morawa). Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the paper (a full-text search for stress/accent/penult = 0).

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1977. The distribution of cultural vocabulary in Papua. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 3, 51-100. PL C-40. doi:10.15144/PL-C40.51 — ADDITIONAL COVERS of the searcher's container 7 found on reading the downloaded file (the searcher listed Bauwaki only).
sources.note: as above; no phonology

sources.citation: Thomson, N. P. 1975. The dialects of Magi. In R. Conrad, W. Dye, N. Thomson & L. Bruce (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18, 37-90. Pacific Linguistics A-40. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A40.37. (Sec. 4.2, items 1-292 of Wurm's modified TRIPP list, cites c.121 Morawa [MMo] forms from Thomson's own Badubadu wordlist.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone for any language: full-text search for stress/accent/penult/syllable/tone/tonal = 0 hits. Morawa forms are cited in plain segmental transcription with glottal stop (e.g. 'MMo egi' man, 'MMo aveha' woman, 'MMo nana' blood, 'MMo kisa' bone, 'MMo lina' sun, 'MMo devene' moon, 'MMo guba' rain), unmarked for stress. Intro pp.37-38: 'None of these languages, except Magi, has ever been described'.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1971. Languages of south-east Papua: a preliminary report. In Dutton, Voorhoeve & Wurm, Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14, 1-46. Pacific Linguistics A-28. (ANU hdl 1885/145019)

sources.citation: Grist, R. W. (Assistant Resident Magistrate, Abau). 1926. Appendix VI. Eastern Division: Languages of the Abau District (paras 778-792, with table 'Distribution of languages spoken in the Abau District') and para 793 'Vocabulary. Abau Station, Eastern Division. Name of tribe -- Morawa. Name of villages -- Duramu, Bada-Bada, Iniado. Situation: Ganai, Cloudy Bay coast, and delta', dated 30 June 1926. In: Territory of Papua. Annual Report for the year 1925-26, pp.92-94. (= Glottolog 'Grist 1926', wordlist.)
sources.note: No phonology content. Prose paras 778-792 give the geographic distribution of Keakara, Hula, Gebi, Abia, Domu, Morawa ('784. Morawa is spoken by the villages in the Cloudy Bay littoral'), Bina-hari, Bauwaki, Nawp (Dimuga), Magori, Magi, note that coastal men also speak Motu, and say introduced words are marked; the c.120-item Morawa vocabulary (p.94) is in plain romanisation with hyphenated syllables (Wagi-alala 'path', Au-taga), loans flagged as Suau/Magi/Motuan; no accents, nothing on stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Bastard, E. M. (officer compiling), compiled [edited] by W. M. Strong. 1918. Vocabularies: Abau Station, Eastern Division. Name of tribe, Morawa. Names of villages, Ganai, Iniado, Duramu, and Badubadu (dated 24 September 1918). In: Papua. Annual Report for the year 1917-18, p.90 (with Lau-una p.89 and Magori/Dimuga p.91; indexed again in the 1918-19 report pp.105-106). (= Glottolog 'Bastard 1918', wordlist; Klieneberger 1957 no. 749.)
sources.note: No phonology content: standard Annual-Report c.120-item list (Rina 'sun', Deweni 'moon', Guba 'rain', Emegi 'man', Aweha 'woman', numerals Mi-au, Sauna, Haunami..), plain romanisation with hyphens, footnotes only '*Native / +European' for tobacco; no accent marks (the two acutes in Capell's manuscript copy, opé and naiá, are not in the printed scanned text and in any case carry no rule), no remark on pronunciation, accent or tone.

sources.citation: [Armit, L. P. B., Resident Magistrate, East-Central Division] 1914. Vocabularies of native languages spoken in East-Central Division: (f) Monoma tribe (villages Eniado, Ogea, Duramu, Badubadu, Gobona -- Cloudy Bay) and Buari tribe. In: Papua. Annual Report for the year 1913-14, pp.190-193. Melbourne: Government Printer. (= Glottolog 'Anonymous 1914', listed by Glottolog as a wordlist, Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for mora1273.)
sources.note: No phonology content: c.400-item English-Monoma-Buari vocabulary with numerals, personal/possessive pronouns and pronominal suffixes (-gu, -mu, -na, -mai, -bo, -veri); forms written in plain romanisation with hyphens at some morpheme/syllable breaks (e.g. Eni-gogo 'thumb', Au-diari 'toes'); no accent marks, no note on pronunciation, accent or tone. (scanned text of HathiTrust seq 198-201 saved as extract.)

sources.citation: [Anonymous; Resident Magistrate, East-Central Division] 1913. Appendix E. Vocabularies of native languages spoken in East-Central Division: Magi tribe (Mailu, Eroro, Darava, Boru, Domara); Monomor tribe (Eniardo, Ogea, Durama -- villages near the coast [Cloudy Bay]); Keveri tribe. In: Papua. Annual Report for the year 1912-13, p.172. Melbourne: Government Printer. (= Glottolog 'Anonymous 1913', listed by Glottolog as a wordlist; Pawley & Hammarstrom 2017 'Anonymous 1913'.)
sources.note: Nothing. One-page three-column vocabulary (c.75 English glosses: arm, arrow, banana, belly, bird.. woman) in plain romanisation with hyphens at some syllable breaks (Mo-o, Bo-ana, U-u-ai, A-a-asoda); no accent marks, no note on pronunciation, accent or tone; unsigned (the 1913-14 continuation is signed L. P. B. Armit, R.M.).
